# Percona Server for MySQL 8.4

> Percona Server for MySQL 8.4, a drop-in replacement for MySQL Community 8.4: what Percona adds or changes, with installation, upgrade, security and operations guides

Each page below is also available as markdown. For the documentation of all Percona products, see https://docs.percona.com/llms.txt.

## Install

- [Install Percona Server for MySQL from repositories](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/installation.md): Before installing, read the Percona Server for MySQL 8.4 Release notes.
- [Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO) and non-PGO builds](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/pgo.md): Starting with Percona Server for MySQL 8.4.10-10, Percona publishes a mixture of Profile-Guided Optimization (PGO) and non-PGO builds. With PGO, the compiler uses profiling data from representative…
- [Percona Software Download instructions](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/download-instructions.md): Do the following steps to select the software:
- [Use APT: Use APT repositories](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/apt-repo.md): Ready-to-use packages are available from the Percona Server for MySQL software repositories and the Percona downloads page.
- [Use APT: DEB package list](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/apt-files.md)
- [Build APT packages](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/build-apt-packages.md): If you wish to build your own Debian/Ubuntu (dpkg) packages of Percona Server for MySQL, you first need to start with a source tarball, either from the Percona website or by generating your own by…
- [Use APT: Downloaded DEB packages](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/apt-download-deb.md): Download the packages from Percona Product Downloads. If needed, Instructions for the Percona Product Download are available.
- [Use APT: Apt pinning](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/apt-pinning.md): Pinning allows you to stay on a release and get packages from a different version. In some cases, you can pin selected packages and avoid accidentally upgrading all the packages.
- [Use APT: Run Percona Server for MySQL](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/apt-run.md): Percona Server for MySQL stores the data files in /var/lib/mysql/ by default. You can find the configuration file that is used to manage Percona Server for MySQL in /etc/mysql/my.cnf.
- [Use APT: Uninstall](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/apt-uninstall-server.md): To uninstall Percona Server for MySQL you’ll need to remove all the installed packages. Removing packages with apt remove does not remove the configuration and data files. Removing the packages with…
- [Use DNF: Install using DNF](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/yum-repo.md): For Docker containers, see Running Percona Server for MySQL in a Docker Container.

- [Use DNF: Run Percona Server for MySQL](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/yum-run.md): Percona Server for MySQL stores the data files in /var/lib/mysql/ by default. The configuration file used to manage Percona Server for MySQL is the /etc/my.cnf.
- [Use DNF: Uninstall](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/yum-uninstall.md): To completely uninstall Percona Server for MySQL, remove all the installed packages and data files.
- [Use binary tarballs: Install with binary tarballs](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/binary-tarball-install.md): A binary tarball is one file that contains the server binaries and support files. The tar command bundles the files, and gzip compresses them.

The generic binary tarball bundles many of those libraries. The DEB and RPM packages link the operating system copies…

- [Common SQL commands](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/common-sql.md): SQL commands used by MySQL can be categorized into different types based on their purposes: Data Definition Language (DDL), Data Manipulation Language (DML), Data Control Language (DCL), and…
- [SELECT statement](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/select.md): The syntax of a SELECT statement in MySQL is straightforward. You start with the keyword SELECT, followed by the columns from which you want to retrieve data. You can specify the table from which to…
- [INSERT statement](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/insert.md): In MySQL, the INSERT statement adds new rows of data to a table. It follows a simple syntax pattern that beginners can easily understand.
- [UPDATE statement](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/update.md): The UPDATE statement modifies existing records in a table.
- [DELETE statement](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/delete.md): The DELETE statement removes one or more rows from a table based on specified conditions. It allows developers to selectively delete data from a table, providing a way to manage and maintain the…
- [SQL operators](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/sql-operators.md): SQL operators are symbols or keywords used to perform operations on data in SQL queries.
- [Common data types](https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/8.4/data-types-basic.md): Choosing the correct data type for each column ensures data accuracy, efficiency, and reliability within the database. The following describes the purpose of a data type in Percona Server for MySQL:
